limitations: Runtime binding proves a pure native scalar wrapper before adding the per-instance context-preservation tag.
The wrapper ABI, signature and lifetime behavior are preserved; Go and cross-instance callbacks retain ordinary context publication.
Both reversed runs compare the exact artifact and contract with 15 timing samples per phase.
Compiler cost uses three alternating pairs of 100 passes over 218 Core3 and 27 thread modules.
Compact import and native thread identity remain slower than the pinned Clang peer.

Opaque owned callback regresses 2.87 and 2.59 percent versus 2cd322f0 in the two reversed runs, remaining roughly twice as fast as 49145ddf; full-snapshot comparison separately measures the combined change.
The first Remote broad run lacked two dynamic funcref fixtures; after copying the checked-in artifacts into the owned cache, the same selector passed.
